heuristics.rule: With a 3-year PGWP, you have 18-24 months to land a TEER 0/1/2/3 role and accumulate 12 months before needing to file for CEC
heuristics.condition: When you are a PGWP holder beginning your post-graduation job search in Canada
heuristics.action: Prioritize getting into any qualifying TEER 0/1/2/3 role quickly over finding the ideal role, treating Phase 1 as timeline management not career optimization
heuristics.because: Every month spent unemployed or in TEER 4/5 work compresses or eliminates the CEC window, forcing reliance on renewal, alternative streams, or leaving Canada

heuristics.rule: Look up the NOC code of any target role before accepting it, not after
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a job offer or targeting a role as a PGWP holder
heuristics.action: Confirm the NOC TEER classification independently — do not rely on the employer's job title or description to infer CEC eligibility
heuristics.because: Misclassified roles where employer calls it technical but NOC codes it as administrative have caused CEC eligibility rejections; a 'Junior IT Analyst' might be TEER 2 not TEER 1 — both eligible, but the distinction must be known before acceptance

heuristics.rule: Pursue Provincial Nomination before any other CRS optimization lever post-March 2025
heuristics.condition: When trying to maximize CRS score after LMIA job offer points were removed
heuristics.action: Target PNP streams first — a single nomination adds 600 CRS points and functionally guarantees an ITA regardless of base CRS score
heuristics.because: No other single action comes close to the 600-point PNP bonus; all other levers (French, additional work experience, education) add at most 25-100 points each

heuristics.rule: Invest in French proficiency before over-investing in English score improvement
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder already has CLB 9+ English and is looking to add CRS points through language
heuristics.action: Study for TEF Canada or TCF Canada French exam instead of retaking IELTS/CELPIP to push English from CLB 9 to CLB 10
heuristics.because: Increasing English from CLB 9 to CLB 10 adds only a few CRS points, while French CLB 7+ adds 25-50 points and unlocks dedicated Francophone draws at cut-offs of ~365-400 versus general draws at ~500

heuristics.rule: Enter the Express Entry pool after 1 year of skilled work, but calculate whether waiting for 2 years is feasible given PGWP expiry
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder has completed 1 year of TEER 0/1/2/3 work and is deciding when to apply
heuristics.action: Compare the 13 additional CRS points gained from a second year of Canadian work experience against the remaining PGWP timeline to determine if waiting is viable
heuristics.because: A second year of Canadian skilled work experience adds ~13 CRS points, which can meaningfully affect ITA timing, but only if PGWP expiry does not create a gap in status

heuristics.rule: If deciding between Ontario and BC for job search, Ontario OINP Masters Graduate stream is more accessible if you hold an Ontario master's degree
heuristics.condition: When a master's graduate is choosing which province to target for both employment and PR pathway
heuristics.action: Prioritize Ontario if you have an Ontario master's degree because the OINP Masters Graduate stream requires no job offer and can be applied for immediately after graduation
heuristics.because: BC PNP Tech requires a job offer in a target NOC code before nomination, adding dependency on employer action; OINP Masters Graduate removes that dependency entirely

heuristics.rule: Do not accept below-market offers due to perceived visa insecurity when on PGWP
heuristics.condition: When negotiating salary as a PGWP holder in Canada
heuristics.action: Negotiate based on market rates using Glassdoor Canada, LinkedIn Salary, or Levels.fyi benchmarks without discounting for immigration status
heuristics.because: PGWP is not employer-specific — unlike H-1B in the US, there is no LCA wage floor but also no employer lock-in, meaning visa insecurity is not a legitimate reason to accept below-market compensation

heuristics.rule: For tech graduates willing to learn French, Montreal offers a faster PR path than Toronto or Vancouver at lower cost of living
heuristics.condition: When a tech graduate is choosing a Canadian city and is open to French language investment
heuristics.action: Target Montreal, develop French to CLB 7+, and use either the Quebec PRTQ pathway or dedicated IRCC Francophone draws at ~365-400 CRS cut-off
heuristics.because: Montreal combines major tech employers (Ubisoft, CAE, Lightspeed, Coveo), lower cost of living than Toronto/Vancouver, and access to lower-cut-off dedicated draws that bypass the general pool competition

heuristics.rule: Time LinkedIn cold outreach to Canadian hiring cycles
heuristics.condition: When conducting cold outreach to Canadian professionals for job search purposes
heuristics.action: Concentrate outreach activity in September-October and January-February, and target hiring managers or senior individual contributors rather than HR recruiters
heuristics.because: Canadian hiring cycles concentrate in these windows, and decision-makers — not HR — are the correct first point of contact for referral-based entry, consistent with effective outreach strategy

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines how much time exists to complete Phase 1 (get TEER-eligible role) and Phase 2 (accumulate 12 months, apply CEC) before status expires
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate months remaining on PGWP; subtract 12 months needed for CEC work experience; the remainder is the maximum Phase 1 job search window

decision_factors.factor: NOC TEER classification of target roles
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Only TEER 0/1/2/3 work experience qualifies for CEC; TEER 4/5 does not count regardless of how skilled or technical the role feels
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look up the specific NOC code on the IRCC NOC finder before accepting any offer; do not rely on employer job title to infer classification

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines PNP stream eligibility — OINP Masters Graduate requires Ontario degree, SINP Graduate requires Saskatchewan institution, BC PNP requires BC job offer
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Match your degree-granting institution's province to available PNP streams; check whether streams require job offer or are nomination-only

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency or willingness to develop it
decision_factors.why_it_matters: French CLB 7+ unlocks dedicated Francophone draws at cut-offs ~100+ points lower than general draws and adds 25-50 direct CRS points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess current French level; estimate time to CLB 7 on TEF Canada; calculate CRS point gain versus time investment against PGWP timeline

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Master's degree unlocks OINP Masters Graduate stream (no job offer required) — one of the most accessible PNP pathways available
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm degree type and Canadian institution; check OINP eligibility requirements for Masters Graduate stream; apply as soon as eligible

decision_factors.factor: Field of study and corresponding NOC codes
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines which TEER levels are accessible and how broad or narrow the qualifying role universe is for CEC accumulation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your field to TEER 0/1/2/3 NOC codes using the quick reference; identify whether adjacent lower-TEER roles (e.g., TEER 2) are acceptable fallbacks

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines how far from the current ITA cut-off you are and which optimization levers are worth pursuing
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use IRCC CRS calculator with current credentials; compare output to recent cut-off history; identify point gap and which levers close it fastest

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Phase 1 success depends on actually getting hired; a strong market reduces Phase 1 duration and preserves more PGWP runway
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare job posting volume in your NOC code across provinces; assess competition level and whether PNP stream in that province requires a job offer

decision_factors.factor: Cost of living in target city
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Financial sustainability during job search affects how long a candidate can hold out for TEER-eligible roles versus accepting TEER 4/5 work for income
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare salary benchmarks against housing and living costs across Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Calgary; Montreal offers best salary-to-cost ratio for tech

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Spending 6-12 months searching exclusively for an ideal role rather than any qualifying TEER 0/1/2/3 role
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: CEC window is compressed or eliminated entirely; candidate must rely on PGWP renewal, alternative streams, or departure from Canada rather than the intended CEC pathway
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PGWP holders who job search like domestic graduates without accounting for the immigration timeline running concurrently

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a role with a job title that sounds technical without verifying the NOC code
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: If the NOC code is administrative rather than technical, work experience accumulated in that role does not count toward CEC eligibility — months of work are wasted for PR purposes
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PGWP holders in roles with ambiguous titles such as 'analyst,' 'coordinator,' or 'associate' where classification is non-obvious

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Targeting BC over Ontario for job search because of higher tech salaries
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: BC PNP Tech requires a job offer before nomination, adding employer dependency to the PR pathway; if job offer doesn't materialize, the PNP advantage is inaccessible — whereas OINP Masters Graduate requires no job offer
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Master's graduates from Ontario institutions who relocate to BC for salary reasons without calculating the PNP access difference

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Entering Express Entry pool after exactly 1 year of skilled work to avoid PGWP expiry risk
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Forfeits approximately 13 additional CRS points from a second year of Canadian work experience, which could lengthen wait time for ITA by months
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PGWP holders whose base CRS score is borderline relative to current cut-offs, where 13 points is the difference between rounds

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Ignoring French language study because primary language is English
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Leaves 25-100 CRS points and access to dedicated Francophone draws (cut-off ~365-400 vs ~500) entirely on the table — potentially adding 12-18 months to ITA wait
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PGWP holders with base CRS scores in the 400-490 range who are waiting for general draw cut-offs to drop

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Targeting Quebec (Montreal) for faster PR via French proficiency
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Quebec operates a completely separate immigration system (CSQ required before federal PR); if French is not strong enough, the Quebec pathway closes and the candidate is not automatically eligible for federal Express Entry from Quebec work experience alone
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates who move to Montreal assuming French effort will automatically translate to faster PR without understanding the bifurcated federal/Quebec system

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on ACCES Employment or Magnet for job search as an international graduate
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: These platforms are valuable but primarily surface traditional employers and nonprofit-adjacent roles; candidates in competitive tech or finance may find the opportunities below market rate or misaligned with NOC TEER 1 targets
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: High-skilled candidates in competitive fields who over-allocate time to newcomer-specific platforms at the expense of direct LinkedIn and referral-based outreach

failure_patterns.pattern: Job searching as a PGWP holder using a domestic graduate mindset — targeting ideal roles only and treating the search as open-ended
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: PGWP holders often do not internalize that immigration timelines run concurrently with job search timelines; the urgency of Phase 1 is not obvious until the window has already closed
failure_patterns.consequence: 6-12 months pass in unemployment or TEER 4/5 work; CEC window compresses; candidate must pursue inferior fallback immigration options or leave Canada
warning_signs: Candidate has been searching 6+ months and has not yet entered a TEER 0/1/2/3 role
Candidate is prioritizing company prestige or role title over NOC classification when evaluating offers

failure_patterns.pattern: Accepting a role without verifying NOC TEER classification, then discovering the role is TEER 4/5 or administratively coded after accumulating months of experience
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates assume employer job titles map directly to TEER classifications; NOC system is not widely understood and verification requires proactive lookup
failure_patterns.consequence: Months of work experience do not count toward CEC eligibility; candidate must restart the 12-month clock with a new qualifying role, further compressing the PGWP window
warning_signs: Candidate has not independently looked up the NOC code for their current or target role
Employer's job description uses broad titles like 'analyst,' 'coordinator,' or 'associate' without referencing specific technical duties

failure_patterns.pattern: Over-investing in English language test preparation to squeeze marginal CRS points from CLB 9 to CLB 10
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: English is the candidate's strongest language and the one they feel most confident improving; the asymmetric return of French investment is not intuitive
failure_patterns.consequence: Time and money spent on IELTS/CELPIP retakes yields only a few CRS points; the same investment in French could yield 25-50 points and dedicated draw eligibility
warning_signs: Candidate is already at CLB 9 English and is preparing to retake IELTS before attempting any French assessment
Candidate is unaware that DELF/DALF does not count for Express Entry

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming a job offer will add points to CRS score and factoring phantom LMIA points into PR timeline planning
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Pre-2025 Express Entry advice widely circulated the 50-200 point LMIA job offer bonus; post-March 2025 removal is not yet reflected in much informal advice
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidate's actual CRS score is significantly lower than planned; ITA timeline extends beyond what was anticipated; PGWP expiry risk increases
warning_signs: Candidate is referencing pre-2025 CRS calculation guides without checking for IRCC updates
Candidate's PR plan depends on receiving a job offer to 'boost' their CRS score

failure_patterns.pattern: Moving to Montreal for tech without adequate French proficiency and without understanding the Quebec-federal immigration bifurcation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Montreal is correctly identified as a high-value market, but candidates conflate 'working in Quebec' with 'qualifying for Quebec immigration streams' and underestimate French requirements
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidate accumulates Quebec work experience that does not translate to a CSQ; must either develop French from scratch mid-career or pivot to federal Express Entry with a Quebec-based job — which still works but loses the dedicated draw advantage
warning_signs: Candidate is relocating to Montreal with no French proficiency and no plan for French development
Candidate does not know the difference between CSQ and federal PR

diagnostic_questions.question: How many months remain on your PGWP, and are you currently in a TEER 0/1/2/3 role?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate's CEC window is still viable or already compromised; determines urgency level of Phase 1 intervention
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How many months have you been in that role? Are you on track to hit 12 months before your PGWP expires with enough runway to file?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How long have you been searching? Have you considered broadening to any TEER 0/1/2/3 role rather than your target role specifically?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you independently looked up the NOC code for your current or target role on the IRCC NOC finder?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has confirmed CEC eligibility of their work experience or is operating on assumption based on job title
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is the NOC code and TEER level? Does your employer's description of your duties match the NOC lead statement?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do this immediately — especially if your title includes words like 'analyst,' 'coordinator,' or 'associate' which can be coded administratively

diagnostic_questions.question: Did you complete your degree at a Canadian institution, and if so, which province — and at what level (master's vs. bachelor's)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines PNP stream eligibility — specifically whether the candidate qualifies for OINP Masters Graduate (no job offer required) or other province-specific graduate streams
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Ontario master's: have you applied to OINP Masters Graduate stream? If not, why not — this is one of the most accessible PNP paths available.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Which province are you currently working in? Check if that province's PNP has a graduate stream for your institution type

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your current French language proficiency level, and have you taken TEF Canada or TCF Canada?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Reveals whether the candidate has assessed or optimized their largest accessible non-PNP CRS lever post-LMIA removal
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What CLB level did you achieve? If CLB 7+ in all four skills, are you aware of dedicated Francophone draws and their lower cut-offs?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you taken any French courses? Estimate time to CLB 7 and calculate whether 25-50 CRS points is worth the investment given your current base score and cut-off gap

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your current estimated CRS score, and how does it compare to the most recent general draw cut-off?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines how large the gap is and which combination of levers can close it within the candidate's PGWP timeline
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If within 50 points: which single lever gets you there fastest — French proficiency, waiting for a second year of work experience, or a PNP stream?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Use the IRCC CRS calculator with your actual credentials before making any optimization decisions

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you currently in Quebec, or are you considering Montreal for your job search?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the candidate needs to understand the Quebec-federal bifurcated immigration system and the CSQ requirement
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is your French level? Do you understand the difference between CSQ, PRTQ, and federal Express Entry? Are you eligible for PRTQ if already employed in Quebec?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: No immediate action — but if considering Montreal, assess French proficiency investment before relocating

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you planning your CRS score around receiving LMIA job offer points?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Identifies whether the candidate is operating on outdated pre-March 2025 information and has an inaccurately high CRS projection
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Recalculate your CRS score immediately using the post-March 2025 framework — LMIA points no longer exist; your actual score may be 50-200 points lower than anticipated
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Confirm you are using the current IRCC CRS calculator and recent cut-off data to set timeline expectations

industry_realities.common_belief: PGWP holders should job search for their ideal role the same way domestic graduates do, using career ambition as the primary filter
industry_realities.actual_reality: PGWP holders are operating a dual-track process where immigration timeline constraints run concurrently with job search; spending 6-12 months for the ideal role can permanently close the CEC pathway
industry_realities.implication: Phase 1 job search should prioritize any qualifying TEER 0/1/2/3 role; ideal role pursuit is a Phase 2 or post-PR activity

industry_realities.common_belief: A job offer from a Canadian employer will significantly boost your CRS score through LMIA points
industry_realities.actual_reality: IRCC removed LMIA-based job offer points from Express Entry in March 2025; a job offer no longer adds 50-200 CRS points to your score
industry_realities.implication: CRS optimization strategy must shift entirely to PNP nomination, French proficiency, and additional Canadian work experience — job offer pursuit as a CRS tactic is now obsolete

industry_realities.common_belief: The best way to add CRS points through language is to improve English test scores
industry_realities.actual_reality: Most PGWP holders already score CLB 9+ in English; the marginal gain from CLB 9 to CLB 10 is minimal, while French CLB 7+ adds 25-50 points and unlocks dedicated draws at cut-offs ~100 points lower than general pool
industry_realities.implication: For candidates already at CLB 9 English, French language investment has dramatically higher ROI than English retesting

industry_realities.common_belief: A 'technical' or 'professional' job title guarantees CEC-eligible skilled worker classification
industry_realities.actual_reality: NOC classification is determined by the duties performed and how IRCC codes that occupational category — not by what the employer calls the role; administrative coding of a technical role has caused CEC rejections
industry_realities.implication: Every PGWP holder must independently verify the NOC code and TEER level of any role they accept before starting to accumulate work experience for CEC

industry_realities.common_belief: Working in Montreal automatically qualifies you for Quebec immigration streams and accelerates PR
industry_realities.actual_reality: Quebec has a completely separate immigration system; CSQ must be obtained through Quebec streams before federal PR can be granted; French is functionally mandatory; working in Quebec on a PGWP does not automatically qualify you for any Quebec stream
industry_realities.implication: Montreal is only a PR-accelerated path for candidates with genuine French proficiency who actively pursue CSQ through PRTQ or QSWP — not passively through employment alone

industry_realities.common_belief: Canadian salary negotiation is constrained by visa status because employers hold leverage over immigration-dependent workers
industry_realities.actual_reality: PGWP is open work permit and not employer-specific; there is no LCA wage floor (unlike H-1B in the US) but also no employer lock-in; visa insecurity is not a legitimate basis for accepting below-market compensation
industry_realities.implication: PGWP holders should negotiate using standard market benchmarks without discounting for immigration status — they have more negotiating flexibility than H-1B holders in the US

industry_realities.common_belief: PNP nomination is an advanced or difficult step reserved for candidates who have been in Canada for years
industry_realities.actual_reality: OINP Masters Graduate stream can be applied for immediately upon graduation from an Ontario master's program with no job offer required; processing is 6-12 months and adds 600 CRS points upon nomination
industry_realities.implication: Master's graduates from Ontario institutions should apply to OINP Masters Graduate stream as soon as they graduate — delaying this application delays the most impactful CRS lever available to them

industry_realities.common_belief: Government job boards and newcomer-specific platforms like Magnet are less legitimate or less effective than LinkedIn for professional roles
industry_realities.actual_reality: Job Bank Canada explicitly flags roles open to PGWP holders; Magnet is purpose-built to connect newcomers with employers who are immigration-status-aware; many large Canadian employers (RBC, TD, Deloitte, KPMG) run formal diversity hiring programs specifically for international graduates
industry_realities.implication: Immigration-aware job boards and employer programs reduce friction in Phase 1 job search and should be used in parallel with LinkedIn outreach rather than dismissed

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Targets only ideal roles matching career ambitions without accounting for NOC TEER classification or immigration timeline; treats job search as purely a career decision
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Treats Phase 1 as timeline management — any TEER 0/1/2/3 qualifying role is acceptable to start the CEC clock; reserves career optimization for Phase 2 or post-PR
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Candidates who optimize for ideal roles in Phase 1 risk losing the CEC window entirely, forcing reliance on inferior fallback immigration pathways

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Assumes employer job title reflects CEC eligibility; does not independently verify NOC code before accepting an offer
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Looks up NOC code on IRCC finder before accepting any offer; confirms duties align with NOC lead statement; treats this as a standard pre-acceptance checklist item
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Unverified NOC classification has caused CEC eligibility rejections after months of accumulated work experience — a costly and avoidable error

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Plans CRS score based on a job offer adding points (LMIA); uses pre-2025 guides or informal advice without checking IRCC updates
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Plans CRS score using the current post-March 2025 framework; prioritizes PNP nomination, French proficiency, and work experience years as the only viable levers
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Operating on outdated LMIA assumptions produces a CRS projection that is 50-200 points too high, leading to a PR timeline that is entirely wrong

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Prepares to retake IELTS or CELPIP to push English score from CLB 9 to CLB 10 as the primary CRS optimization move
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Recognizes marginal English gain is minimal at CLB 9+ and redirects effort to French proficiency (TEF Canada/TCF Canada) for 25-50 CRS points and dedicated Francophone draw access
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: The ROI difference between English retesting and French development at CLB 9 English is dramatic; misallocating study time to English can add 12-18 months to ITA wait

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Chooses province based on salary levels or personal preference without mapping PNP stream requirements to their specific profile
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Maps PNP stream eligibility to personal profile first (degree level, institution province, job offer status) and lets PR pathway accessibility be a primary input to provincial targeting
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A master's graduate from Ontario who moves to BC for higher salaries may forfeit OINP Masters Graduate access (no job offer required) in exchange for BC PNP Tech (job offer required) — a materially worse PR position

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Accepts below-market offers because of perceived employer leverage stemming from visa dependency; conflates PGWP constraints with H-1B-style employer lock-in
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Negotiates using market benchmarks (Glassdoor Canada, LinkedIn Salary, Levels.fyi); understands PGWP is open and not employer-specific; does not discount compensation for immigration status
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Accepting below-market offers due to misunderstood visa constraints costs candidates real money and sets a lower salary baseline for future negotiation

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Identifies Montreal as a good market and assumes working there will accelerate PR through vague association with French/Quebec immigration advantages
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Evaluates Quebec pathway only if French proficiency is at CLB 7+ or can realistically be reached; understands CSQ vs. federal PR distinction; considers PRTQ eligibility specifically
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Relocating to Montreal without French proficiency or understanding of the Quebec-federal bifurcation produces accumulated Quebec work experience that does not automatically unlock any PR acceleration
